items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: He said I was going to let Hobart have Benny Goodman-- let Benny Goodman have Hobart

ctx.x: That's what I found out, and so anyway, I hired Amos back, put him in there and we left for New York and when we got in we did a couple of sessions and no trouble whatsoever with Amos, and one of the numbers where Amos did solo, he was responsible for the T Town Blues being as big a hit as it was, and if it had really been pushed, I think it would have been a national hit. Amos, frankly, did all of the solo work that we did on all the records; Amos did all the solo work. And if we have a chance before we send…

When I got to New York, another-- now he said how much he thought of him but I didn't know he thought as much of him as he did, was Hobart Banks, the piano player. We got there and Hammond said, where's Hobart? I said Hobart wouldn't come. He said, if you would have brought Hobart, you and Hobart both would have been the happiest two men, nobody could have been any happier. So I said what's up. He said I was going to let Hobart have Benny Goodman-- let Benny Goodman have Hobart, and I said, let him go to Benny…
He'd give you five thousand dollars?
